actions.label: WHO's Emergency Committee assessed the Angola and DRC urban yellow-fever outbreaks as serious public-health events requiring intensified national action and enhanced international support.

aliases: 2016 Angola Yellow Fever Regional Epidemic and Biosecurity Event
canonical_event.name: Angola Yellow Fever Outbreak of 2016
canonical_event.summary: Angola Yellow Fever Outbreak of 2016 was a real regional-epidemic or biosecurity event involving localized outbreaks, cross-border transmission risk, biosurveillance, or laboratory-related controversy.

episodes.label: Outbreak First Detected in Luanda, Angola
episodes.summary: A yellow fever outbreak was first detected in Luanda, Angola in late December 2015, marking the start of the 2016 Angola yellow fever epidemic.

episodes.label: Laboratory Confirmation of Initial Yellow Fever Cases
episodes.summary: Initial yellow fever cases from the December 2015 Luanda, Angola outbreak were confirmed by two reference laboratories: the National Institute for Communicable Diseases (South Africa) on 19 January 2016 and the Institut Pasteur Dakar on 20 January 2016.

episodes.label: Rapid Case Surge and Initial Local Vaccination Campaign
episodes.summary: After yellow fever outbreak cases in Luanda Angola were confirmed in mid-January 2016, a rapid surge in cases occurred, with 240 reported infections and 51 deaths by Feb 15 2016, and initial local vaccination campaigns were rolled out in Luanda targeting 1.6 million residents, with over 450,000 people vaccinated as of mid-February 2016.

episodes.label: Cross-Border Transmission Risk Emergence
episodes.summary: During the 2016 Angola yellow fever outbreak, confirmed cases were exported cross-border to the Democratic Republic of Congo, China, and Kenya, raising regional and international transmission risk assessed by WHO's Emergency Committee in mid-May 2016

episodes.label: First WHO IHR Emergency Committee Meeting on Yellow Fever Outbreak
episodes.summary: The first WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting for the 2016 yellow fever outbreak was held via teleconference on 19 May 2016. The committee assessed outbreaks in Angola and DRC, deemed them a serious public health event requiring intensified national action and international support, and concluded they did not constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) at the time.

episodes.label: Scaled Mass Vaccination and Vector Control Implementation
episodes.summary: Following the first WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting on 19 May 2016, scaled mass yellow fever vaccination campaigns and vector control measures were implemented across Angola and the Democratic Republic of Congo to contain the 2015-2016 outbreak, with over 16 million people vaccinated using standard and fractional dosing strategies amid global vaccine supply constraints.

episodes.label: Second WHO IHR Emergency Committee Meeting on Yellow Fever Outbreak
episodes.summary: Second WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting held via teleconference on 31 August 2016 to assess yellow fever outbreak status in Angola, DRC, and at-risk regions, concluding the outbreak does not constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern but remains a serious public health event requiring continued national action and international support.

episodes.label: Uganda Declares End of Related Yellow Fever Outbreak
episodes.summary: On 6 September 2016, Uganda's Ministry of Health declared the end of its 2016 yellow fever outbreak after no active transmission was recorded between 1 June and 30 June 2016; the outbreak caused 3 deaths and 7 confirmed infections, with ongoing surveillance maintained to detect future outbreaks and mitigate importation risks.

episodes.label: Ongoing Post-Outbreak Biosecurity Surveillance
episodes.summary: Post-2016 yellow fever outbreak biosecurity surveillance continues in Uganda and at-risk regions to detect new cases, minimize cross-border importation risk, and monitor ongoing transmission potential.

outcomes.label: The assessment established that intensified national action and enhanced international support were warranted for the outbreaks.

stages.label: Initial Detection and Laboratory Confirmation Stage
stages.summary: This stage spans the period from late December 2015 to 20 January 2016, covering the initial detection of a yellow fever outbreak in Luanda, Angola followed by formal laboratory confirmation of the first associated cases.

stages.label: Case Surge and Local Containment Implementation Stage
stages.summary: Following official laboratory confirmation of the 2016 Angola yellow fever outbreak in mid-January 2016, the stage opened with a rapid surge in reported cases, with 240 infections and 51 deaths recorded by February 15 2016; local health authorities collaborated with the WHO to roll out an initial vaccination campaign in Luanda targeting 1.6 million residents, with over 450,000 people vaccinated by mid-February 2016.

stages.label: International Emergency Assessment and Scaled Response Stage
stages.summary: The stage commences with the first WHO IHR Emergency Committee meeting for the 2016 yellow fever outbreak on 19 May 2016, which assessed the outbreaks in Angola and DRC as a serious public health event requiring intensified national action and enhanced international support, while concluding they did not constitute a Public Health Emergency of International Concern (PHEIC) at that time.

stages.label: Outbreak Containment and Post-Event Surveillance Stage
stages.summary: This Outbreak Containment and Post-Event Surveillance stage commences on 1 September 2016, immediately following the second WHO Emergency Committee meeting held on 31 August 2016; as of the stage onset, no confirmed yellow fever cases had been reported in Angola since 23 June 2016 and in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) since 12 July 2016, with the WHO Emergency Committee confirming the regional outbreaks remain a serious public health event requiring sustained national action and international support.
